docs.title: Team Charter
docs.text:
“Our mission is to refine and optimize our design by creating a collaborative environment where we can sharpen our engineering skills together. We are committed to making our design improve worker efficiency and safety by demonstrating a thorough engineering process.”

Our team gained valuable experience last semester, not only in our engineering skills, but also in project management and documentation. We plan to build on and apply these skills to help streamline the development process and make sure that not only do we deliver a good product, but also document our research to a professional standard. Previously, Sundt has expressed great interest in our pipe inspector concept. We plan to leverage our experience to design a fully functional device that our industry partners can use in a real world construction environment. This would in turn help us gather interest from and friendly relationships with other industry professionals. As a team, we hope to further hone our engineering skills across multiple disciplines such as mechanical engineering, software engineering, and electrical engineering. We expect that this project will serve as a good foundation for future iterations of this robot and become a highlight in our engineering portfolios.

docs.title: Product Mission Statement
docs.text:
"Design and build a small diameter pipe inspection device for Sundt Construction to accelerate construction time and improve safety while reducing worker load."

Our team is committed to improving upon and further developing the autonomous pipe inspection vehicle we developed last semester for Sundt construction. Building on the existing design, we will focus on improving vehicle stability, mobility, reliability, autonomous capabilities, and inspection technology.The vehicle is designed to navigate through small electrical conduits and collect inspection data using onboarding sensors and imaging technology. Through collaboration, engineering, and hands-on problem solving. Our goal is to develop a safe, reliable, and functional vehicle that improves inspection efficiency and reduces construction costs. This project will provide a practical solution for Sundt construction while establishing a strong foundation for future development and continued improvement.

docs.title: Concept Generation and Design Ideation
docs.text:
The goal of our project is to create an autonomous robot that can inspect 4inch diameter pipes and report any faults it finds. These faults include debris in the pipe, water leakage, or collapsed sections. The robot needs to be able to survey the straight line conduit reliably and completely autonomously to free up workers to finish other tasks. Our audience is Sundt construction who has shown interest in this specific design and has highlighted its ideal use cases for us. They have specific parameters they want met such as the pipe diameter, pipe length and expected obstacles. We are also building with the individual workers in mind as we want to make operating the robot as easy as possible and not disrupt their workflow on the jobsite. While Sundt has shown interest in the project its uses are for any other construction or inspection company as well. We are also building the project with the EGR 314 teaching staff in mind as this will also serve as a demonstration of our engineering skills.

(insert Links to appendix for design process images)

docs.title: Design Concept
docs.text:
Our concept sketch shows an ideal design for the task Sundt has asked of us. We decided that using treads would be the optimal system for moving through the pipes as they would be able to easily traverse over any small pieces of debris that might be in the pipe without getting the robot stuck. It also allows for the robot to turn in place should it be in a large enough pipe or possibly turn around corners. The large high resolution camera in the sketch would be the “eyes” of our robot as it would be the primary method of fault detection in the pipe using onboard machine learning to recognize cracks or blockages in the pipe. This would be supported by an array of LEDs which will light up the pipe in order for the robot to have the best possible view of the pipe interior. To keep the robot moving straight we are using a combination of a gyroscope and lidar array to measure the exact angle and speed the robot moves at in order to avoid it veering off course or getting stuck. To power it we will use a rechargeable lithium ion battery which will be easy to use for any worker. All of these features are controlled through the ESP32 microprocessor onboard the robot. Route programming, timing, and results reporting will be handled through a companion app on the operator’s phone or tablet.

The project functionality will be divided between three teammates. Max will be responsible for the treads, wheel encoder motor, and gyroscope, focusing on the movement, distance measurement, and orientation. Will will be responsible for image recognition, improved camera, and lidar sensor, focusing on collecting visual information and detecting useful information about the condition of the pipe. Kurt will be responsible for the contact switch, rechargeable battery, and power supply, while also working with will on transferring collected results wirelessly to an operator’s phone or computer. The backup string and long, low-profile chassis will be a team effort because these features affect the overall physical design and integration of the robot.

The robot will not depend on an internet connection while operating underground. Instead , the ESP32 will collect and store the inspection information as the robot travels through the pipe. Afterward, the collected results can be wirelessly transferred to a nearby phone or computer for the operator to review. This allows the robot to work underground without requiring any internet connection. The human-machine interface will primarily be through an app, with collected visual data and time stamps that allows the operator to examine any issues in the pipes. The robot will also have a physical power switch and a button or switch to deploy the robot for inspection. The sensors and actuator system will allow the ESP32 to control the robot’s movement and response to information from the sensors.

The robot will provide several cues to make it easier to use. The app can display information such as battery level, distance traveled, inspection status, and sensor readings. Clearly labeled buttons will help the operator understand what each function does. Warnings can notify the operator when the robot encounters an obstruction or any other problems within the pipe. The app will guide the user through the inspection process and any route programming needed for their pipe system.

docs.title: Vision System
docs.text: Solution Pros Cons Price REALTEK AMB82 MINI IOT AI CAMERA - On-board AI object detection software- Wide-angle lens allows for full vision of pipe ahead- High-resolution camera with fast frame rates allows for quick real-time object detection - Focal length is non-adjustable and set for long distance- Short custom data cable means the entire module will need a unique mounting solution $30 OV5640 CAMERA XIAO ESP32S3 SENSE - Familiarity with platform allows for more focus on object detection development time- Long data cable allows for better mounting solution- High resolution with fast frame rates- Minimum focal length is about 10 cm, allowing for better inspection of small pipes- Low cost- Uses ESP32-S3 chip for on-board object detection - Less RAM than other options $24 M5Stack - Highest processing power of any option- High resolution and high frame-rate video- On-board object-detection models preconfigured for common applications - Bulky- Way out of budget- High power cost $95

docs.title: Choice
docs.text: OV5640 CAMERA XIAO ESP32S3 SENSE — upgrade to previously used module

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: The camera provides excellent video resolution and frame rate at a very low cost compared to the other options. It is also familiar to our team, so it will cut down on the amount of time needed to write the necessary software.

docs.title: Drive System
docs.text: Solution Pros Cons Price NFP-GM25-310-OEN - True optical encoder- Stronger than N20- 360 CPR provides good feedback- 3.3/5 V encoder interface- Multiple gear ratios- Compact enough for the pipe robot- Good balance of speed and torque - Larger than N20- Heavier than N20- 4 mm shaft- 7.4 V rather than 5 V- More expensive than basic N20 motors $15 Planetary Gear Motor with Optical Encoder - Very high torque- Planetary gearbox- Optical encoder- Available in 6 V- Excellent for heavier robots- Strong gearbox- Good positional accuracy - 36 mm diameter- Much heavier- Could be difficult to fit inside a 4-inch pipe- Higher current requirements- More expensive $20 GM37-520 - High torque- Metal gearbox- Optical encoder versions available- Many gear ratios- Good for heavier robots- Stronger shaft and gearbox - 37 mm diameter- Large for a 4-inch pipe- Heavy- Typically 12 V- Higher power consumption- More motor than the robot probably needs $40 ROB-28633 - Compact and lightweight- Built-in Hall-effect encoder- 882 counts/revolution- Good speed and torque for its size- 31.5:1 gear ratio- Good for ESP32 control- Fits well in a 4–6 inch pipe - Encoder is magnetic, not optical- Limited torque compared with larger motors- Wheel slip can affect distance accuracy- Small gearbox can be damaged if stalled- Requires a motor driver $9.90

docs.title: Choice
docs.text: SparkFun ROB-28633 N20 Motor With Encoder

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: The ROB-28633 was selected because its compact N20 form factor makes it well suited for the 4–6 inch pipe inspection robot. The integrated Hall-effect encoder provides 882 counts per revolution for accurate motor speed and distance feedback. Its 31.5:1 gear ratio provides a good balance between speed and torque, while its small size and low weight help keep the robot compact and maneuverable. The motor is also compatible with the ESP32 control system and is available as a matched pair for the two-wheel drive system.

docs.title: Drive Sensing
docs.text: Solution Pros Cons Price MicoAir MTF-02P - Optical flow + range in one- 6 m range- Very small and lightweight- 5 V operation- 50 Hz output- UART communication - More expensive than basic optical-flow sensors- Requires UART programming- Optical flow requires adequate lighting $28 Holybro PMW3901 - Small and lightweight- Good optical-flow tracking- 95 Hz output- UART interface- Low power consumption- Easy to integrate - No built-in distance sensor- Requires a separate range sensor- Less functionality than the MTF-02P $20.59 Holybro H-Flow - Optical flow + distance sensor- Up to 30 m range- Built-in 6-axis IMU- Works in low-light conditions- CAN/DroneCAN communication- Very capable sensor - Much more expensive- Heavier at 15.2 g- More complicated than needed- Larger than the MTF-02P $145

docs.title: Choice
docs.text: MicoAir Optical Flow & Range Sensor MTF-02P

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: The MTF-02P was selected because it combines optical flow and distance measurement into one compact and lightweight sensor. Its 6 m range, 50 Hz output, and 5 V operation make it well suited for the pipe inspection robot. Using one sensor for both functions reduces the number of components and saves space, while providing movement and distance data that can work with the N20 motor encoders to improve the robot’s navigation and return-to-start accuracy.

docs.title: Chassis
docs.text: Solution Pros Cons Price Mini RC Truck, 1:64 Scale Monster Truck - Fits within 4-inch pipe with its cosmetics attached- Allows room to attach components with cosmetic shell removed- Trailer hitch can be used to attach rescue line without modification- Off-road tires allow for easy traversal of pipes - Uses generic remote with limited range (30 m)- Limited battery life (20 minutes)- High price means only one can be bought for prototyping $18 each Mini RC Truck, 1:64 Scale Monster Truck Remote Control Car with Lights - Allows more room to attach components with cosmetic shell removed- Trailer hitch can be used to attach rescue line without modification- Off-road tires allow for easy traversal of pipes- Can use phone app instead of remote - Taller than needed (4.1 inches)- Uses generic remote with limited range (30 m)- Limited battery life (20 minutes)- High price means only one can be bought for prototyping- Phone app has very limited range $19 each 2.4GHz Mini RC Tank Toy with LED and Rotating Turret - Flat chassis allows for stable platform to build from- Rotating turret could be utilized to give a 360° camera view- Treads allow for easier traversal of rough terrain - High price point makes any testing or modification risky because duplicates cannot be afforded- Turret mechanism is difficult to disassemble carefully- Paying for unneeded features such as speakers $23 each

docs.title: Choice
docs.text: 2.4 GHz Mini RC Tank Chassis

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: The tank chassis was selected because its treads provide better traction and reduce slipping compared to wheeled chassis. The flat chassis provides a stable platform for mounting the ESP32, motor driver, sensors, and battery, while the compact design allows the robot to traverse rough and uneven surfaces inside the pipe.

docs.title: Motor Controller
docs.text: Solution Pros Cons Price DRV8833PWPR - Surface-mount HTSSOP package- Controls 2 DC motors- 1.5 A output per channel- Compact and lightweight- Works directly with ESP32 PWM signals- Low cost - Motor supply limited to 10.8 V- Less current capability than DRV8848 $3.02 TB6612FNG - Surface-mount 24-SSOP package- Controls 2 DC motors- Up to 1 A continuous per channel- Motor voltage up to 13.5 V- Low power consumption- Inexpensive - Larger package than DRV8833- Lower current capability- Operating temperature is only -20°C to 85°C $2.04 DRV8848PWPR - Surface-mount HTSSOP package- Controls 2 DC motors- Up to 2 A per bridge / 4 A parallel- Motor voltage 4–18 V- More current capacity and voltage headroom- Built-in protection features - More capability than the small N20 motors require- Slightly more expensive- More complex than necessary for this project $2.97

docs.title: Choice
docs.text: DRV8833PWPR Motor Driver

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: The DRV8833PWPR was selected because it can operate with a 5 V motor supply, supports two DC motors, and can be soldered directly to the PCB using its surface-mount package. Its compact size, low cost, and compatibility with the ESP32 make it well suited for controlling the two N20 motors while keeping the robot’s electronics compact.
